target.title: fix: stop doctor misreporting trusted-proxy gateways as unauthenticated
target.body:
Closes #91284

AI-assisted: yes (Codex). I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators running a LAN-bound Gateway with complete trusted-proxy authentication would see doctor report the Gateway as “without authentication” and recommend generating a token. That was inaccurate and could steer operators away from their intended reverse-proxy security boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now recognizes trusted-proxy authentication only when the configuration can satisfy the same startup and request-authorization contracts used by the Gateway. The check remains deliberately conservative: proxy sources must be usable host-scoped addresses (an exact address, `/32`, or `/128`), and enabled Control UI access must use explicit, non-wildcard browser origins.

Missing or invalid identity headers, unusable `allowUsers`, shared-token conflicts, subnets/default routes, non-unicast sources, disallowed loopback sources, host-interface sources, interface-inspection failures, and missing or wildcard Control UI origins all remain `CRITICAL`.

This changes doctor classification and remediation only. It does not change runtime authentication, config/schema, or protocol behavior.

## User Impact

Operators with a complete, host-scoped trusted-proxy deployment now receive an accurate exposure warning with proxy/firewall guidance instead of a false unauthenticated critical and token-repair advice. Unsafe or incomplete deployments still fail closed with a specific critical finding.

## Evidence

Exact head: `7182103f9a0f5dccd913da8fdaceedb7646124ec`

A synthetic, isolated-home before/after VHS recording shows:

- baseline `upstream/main@faf3dbd`: doctor reports the LAN-bound Gateway as unauthenticated and suggests token repair;
- patched exact head: doctor reports trusted-proxy authentication as configured, retains the network-exposure warning, and gives proxy/firewall guidance;
- only RFC 5737 test data and `https://control.example.test` are used.

The 1400×900 recording was decoded frame-by-frame and visually/privacy audited. It contains no local paths, personal identifiers, credentials, or private-network details.

- GIF SHA-256: `c4f759e59ead71c865e003aad5d250867221d93bcb793de3f8aebba380f2b20b`
- MP4 SHA-256: `f0aefe5e8c53f99bfcba3f62eee8cc21406bbdc5811a0c9712e474ee45523908`

Exact-head verification:

- Node 24.15: 180 focused tests passed (111 Gateway auth/runtime-config + 69 doctor security).
- Changed-surface gate passed: formatting, lint, core and core-test typechecks, dependency/API/boundary guards, database-first/media/sidecar guards, and zero runtime import cycles.
- Commit-mode autoreview: `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported`.
- Independent whole-surface review: no P1/P2 findings; the patch delegates to the existing runtime owner instead of reimplementing authorization.

Boundary: the VHS proves doctor classification and remediation. It does not claim a live remote reverse-proxy login flow.
